newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bid for NZ Warriors rugby league club declared.
newsitem.headline: Bid for NZ Warriors rugby league club declared.

text.p: A group of New Zealand rugby league identities are in negotiation with Auckland businessman Roger Bhatnagar to bring together a bid to purchase 100 percent of the Auckland Warriors Super League club, a spokesman for the group said on Thursday.

Former New Zealand coach and current television commentator Graham Lowe said he and ex-Kiwi forward Dean Lonergan and international public relations group owner Malcolm Boyle had been working on a proposal to buy the Warriors for the past three months.
Lowe said the three had approached Bhatnagar when they learned of his interest in acquiring the club. Discussions had continued for several weeks.
Lowe said an offer would be put to the Auckland Rugby League board of control regardless of the involvement of Bhatnagar.
"Dean, Malcolm and I have done an extensive amount of research and preparatory work, and we're almost ready to make a formal offer to the board," Lowe said in a statement.

"Obviously we'd very much like to have Roger Bhatnagar as part of our group, but we'll push on regardless. We represent a huge amount of experience in rugby league, and we believe this bid is essential for the survival and future prosperity of the club."
The Warriors, who are sponsored by brewer DB Group, are languishing at the bottom of the Super League competition table.
"We have every confidence that the Warriors can be turned into a successful enterprise both on and off the field," Lowe said.

"Our aim is to re-affirm the 'New Zealandness' of the Warriors, and our commitment is to seek and develop the very best of New Zealand talent, only looking at non-New Zealand players when such talent is not otherwise available."
The Warriors club was recently independently valued at around NZ$3 million.
